public_payload.normalized_proposition: Every company promising 'AI agents' is really just trying to rebrand chatbots and provide a front-end that connects them to data sources and gives them guardrails.

statement.excerpt: Every company promising "AI agents" is really just trying to rebrand the concept of chatbots and provide a front-end to let you connect them to data sources and give them guardrails so they don't scream curse words at your customers or write poetry about how bad the company is.

from_speaker: really just trying to rebrand the concept of chatbots
our_interpretation: The contextual scope is enterprise SaaS vendors promising AI agents, including the vendors named nearby.
I read rebranding as a claim about the substance of their offerings, rather than an independently measurable claim about executives' private motives.
The plain reading is that all these offerings were limited to chatbot functionality with data connections and controls. A demonstrated counterexample would defeat every.
For this ongoing observation, I use the September 2024 announcement cycle through publication. Earlier announcements are background evidence.
Every company is a scope restriction, not a forecast antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently complete contemporary inventory shows that the relevant offerings were functionally limited to chatbots with data access and guardrails.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one relevant offering demonstrably performed substantive agent work beyond that reduction, such as independently initiating and completing a workflow rather than merely conducting a data-grounded conversation.
